items.title: Pay import charges for held parcel (likely scam)
items.computation: Fixed calendar date printed in the letter: 09.11.2026. It is a Monday and not a public holiday in NW, so no shift. Due date is as written. The letter shows strong scam signs, so do not pay before verifying.

warnings: Likely a scam: real customs fees are not collected by bank transfer to a private company such as 'Intl. Parcel Clearing Ltd.'; genuine import VAT is charged by the carrier or German customs (Zoll).
The letter names no real carrier such as DHL, DPD or Hermes, and gives no customs reference or assessment notice.
Questions are accepted only via WhatsApp and a free-mail-style address (clearance-mail.example), which is a typical phishing pattern.
The deadline is very short (Monday 09.11.2026, four days after the letter's date), and it threatens return or destruction of the parcel to create pressure.
The salutation is generic and does not match a real order. Only pay if you are expecting a parcel from outside the EU, and check the tracking number on the carrier's official website first.
Do not pay, and do not contact the WhatsApp number. If you already paid, contact your bank quickly and consider reporting it to the police or the Verbraucherzentrale.
